name: Securities Markets (MNPI, SEC Reg FD, SOX)
description: Securities-market overlay for agents handling material non-public information (MNPI). Provides full 26-control AKSI coverage with citations to SEC Regulation FD, SOX §302/§404/§802, SEC Cybersecurity Disclosure Rules, and SEC Rule 17a-4. Covers all control domains: governance, identification, protection, detection, response, and recovery. Addresses AI agent-specific MNPI risks including selective disclosure, market manipulation, and insider information leakage through automated workflows.

evidence_requirements: Access to MNPI workflows is limited to approved issuer, legal, finance, and investor-relations identities with multi-factor authentication enforced
Periodic access reviews confirm dormant, orphaned, and over-privileged identities cannot retrieve or disclose market-moving information
Disclosure-owner assignments document which accountable humans may approve, supervise, or revoke MNPI-handling permissions
Least-privilege entitlements and information barriers are enforced between insider teams and external-facing communication workflows
Provisioning and recertification records show only authorized roles can query, summarize, or prepare dissemination of MNPI
Watchlist, restricted-list, or disclosure-window controls are reflected in system entitlements before market-sensitive actions are allowed
Approved data sources, prompts, and model workflows for MNPI analysis are versioned and reviewed before production use
Change records show disclosure logic, summarization prompts, and external distribution paths undergo control-owner review before release
Release approvals tie provenance checks to accountable disclosure, legal, or compliance reviewers for market-sensitive systems
Outbound responses, generated artifacts, and integrated channels are scanned for unauthorized MNPI disclosure before release
Distribution workflows require explicit approval for any external communication that could constitute investor or analyst disclosure
Communication-channel reviews verify public, simultaneous disclosure paths are used when disclosure is permitted
Tamper-evident logs capture every access, summarization, approval, and disclosure action involving MNPI
Retention schedules preserve disclosure-control and access evidence for seven years to support SOX-aligned recordkeeping expectations
Audit trails connect access to approved business purpose, disclosure status, and downstream dissemination decisions
PR-05.framework_reference: SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.100-103; SOX §302, §404, §802; SEC Rule 17a-4

evidence_requirements: Monitoring detects unusual access patterns, bulk exports, or attempted dissemination of MNPI outside approved windows or channels
Escalation runbooks route selective-disclosure, insider-risk, and anomalous-access signals to legal, compliance, and investor-relations owners
Incident records document triage, containment, public-disclosure decisions, and corrective actions for MNPI handling events
DE-01.framework_reference: SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.100(a); SOX §302, §404; SEC Rule 17a-4

evidence_requirements: MNPI governance policy documented and approved by disclosure committee or senior compliance officer; policy covers AI agent handling of market-sensitive information per SOX §302/§404
Policy reviewed at minimum annually and following material incidents, regulatory changes, or significant changes to AI agent capabilities
AI agent use in MNPI workflows formally authorized in governance documentation with defined scope, permitted actions, and oversight requirements
GOV-01.framework_reference: SOX §302, §404; SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.100-103; SEC Cybersecurity Rules 17 CFR 229.106

evidence_requirements: Disclosure committee composition and authority documented; members identified by name and role with explicit accountability for MNPI handling decisions (SOX §302)
Segregation of duties between MNPI-handling AI agent operators and disclosure decision-makers documented and enforced
Compliance and legal oversight roles for AI agent supervision in MNPI contexts defined with reporting lines to executive management and audit committee (SOX §404)
Risk assessment conducted for AI agent components handling MNPI; insider trading, selective disclosure, and market manipulation scenarios assessed (SOX §404)
MNPI risk register maintained covering AI agent failure modes, data leakage vectors, and unauthorized disclosure pathways
Risk assessment incorporated into annual SOX internal control evaluation; findings drive remediation in internal control environment
GOV-03.framework_reference: SOX §404; SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.100(b); SEC Cybersecurity Rules 17 CFR 229.106(b)

evidence_requirements: Human review gate mandated before any AI agent output involving MNPI reaches external parties or influences investor communications (SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.101(e))
Disclosure committee review documented for any AI-assisted investor communication or earnings material involving material non-public information
Automated disclosure workflows require manual approval from designated disclosure officer before transmission; approval records preserved per SOX §802
GOV-04.framework_reference: SOX §302, §404; SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.101(e); SEC Cybersecurity Rules 17 CFR 229.106

evidence_requirements: Inventory of AI agent components with access to MNPI data sources, systems, or workflows maintained; inventory includes model versions, tool integrations, and data connection scope (SOX §404)
MNPI data systems and repositories inventoried; each system classified by sensitivity and disclosure restriction status
Inventory reviewed quarterly or when AI agent capabilities or MNPI data sources change materially
Information barriers (Chinese walls) implemented between MNPI-holding AI agent workflows and external-facing communication systems; boundary controls documented
Network and application segmentation prevents MNPI from flowing to unauthorized systems; data flow diagrams show MNPI containment boundaries (SOX §404)
External access controls verified — investor relations, sell-side analysts, and media channels blocked from direct MNPI system access
MNPI classification procedures applied to all data accessed by AI agents; data classified as material, non-public, or restricted with handling instructions per SEC Reg FD
AI agent context windows and memory scoped to minimum necessary MNPI; access restrictions documented and enforced
Data handling procedures govern how AI agents process earnings data, M&A information, and other MNPI categories; retention and purge schedules defined
Third-party AI service providers with potential MNPI exposure assessed for disclosure risk; contractual confidentiality obligations documented
Model provider agreements prohibit training on customer MNPI data; data processing terms reviewed by legal and compliance
Subprocessors handling MNPI workflows identified; flow-down restrictions equivalent to primary regulatory obligations included in contracts (SOX §404)
Risk profile for each AI agent with MNPI access documented: data categories accessible, authorized action scope, and potential disclosure impact (SOX §404)
AI agent risk profiling includes insider trading and market manipulation scenario analysis specific to each agent's MNPI access scope
Risk profiles reviewed quarterly and updated when agent capabilities, data access scope, or regulatory guidance changes materially
AI agent output filtering prevents generation or transmission of MNPI-derived content to unauthorized recipients or channels (SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.100(a))
Disclosure window controls enforced at agent output layer — agent cannot transmit earnings-sensitive content outside of approved quiet-period and disclosure windows
Content filtering rules reviewed by legal and compliance quarterly; filter bypass events logged and investigated
MNPI data minimization enforced in AI agent workflows — only MNPI necessary for the approved business purpose is ingested; excess scope documented and approved by compliance (SOX §404)
AI agent context and memory purge procedures ensure MNPI is not retained beyond the authorized session or task scope
Data-in-transit encryption applied to all MNPI flows between AI agent components; unencrypted MNPI transmission blocked
Input validation applied to MNPI-handling AI agent workflows; prompt injection and data poisoning attack patterns included in threat model (SOX §802)
Adversarial input detection monitoring deployed on AI agents with MNPI access; alerts generated for anomalous or potentially manipulative inputs
Security testing of MNPI-handling AI agent inputs conducted periodically; test cases cover disclosure-coercion and market manipulation input scenarios (SEC Rule 17a-4)
PR-08.framework_reference: SOX §802; SEC Rule 17a-4; SEC Cybersecurity Rules 17 CFR 229.106

evidence_requirements: Continuous monitoring of AI agent MNPI access patterns; automated alerts for anomalous data access volumes, off-hours activity, or unusual output distribution (SOX §404)
Compliance monitoring program reviews AI agent MNPI handling controls at minimum quarterly; monitoring results documented and escalated
Internal audit coverage includes AI agent MNPI workflows; audit findings and remediation tracked through SOX internal control program
Annual SOX §404 assessment includes evaluation of AI agent controls in MNPI handling workflows; external auditor sign-off documented
Internal control testing covers AI agent access controls, output filtering, and disclosure workflow approval gates (SOX §404)
Penetration testing or red team exercises include MNPI exfiltration scenarios targeting AI agent components; findings drive remediation (SEC Cybersecurity Rules)
Audit log analysis identifies unusual MNPI access patterns, bulk data retrievals, and unauthorized output generation attempts (SOX §404, §802)
Threat intelligence feeds inform detection of market manipulation and insider trading attack patterns relevant to AI agent MNPI workflows (SEC Rule 17a-4)
Behavioral analytics or equivalent monitoring detects deviations from normal AI agent MNPI access and output patterns; alerts reviewed by compliance
Incident response plan covers AI agent MNPI disclosure incidents: unauthorized dissemination, selective disclosure, and suspected market manipulation (SOX §302, §404)
Regulatory notification procedures documented for material cybersecurity incidents affecting MNPI systems per SEC Cybersecurity Rules (4-business-day 8-K disclosure requirement)
Incident response exercises include MNPI breach scenarios; exercise results and plan updates documented annually
RS-01.framework_reference: SOX §302, §404; SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.100(a); SEC Cybersecurity Rules 17 CFR 229.106

evidence_requirements: Human escalation matrix for MNPI incidents identifies disclosure committee, legal, CFO, and investor relations contacts with response authority (SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.101(e))
SEC Form 8-K notification procedure documented for material cybersecurity incidents; 4-business-day disclosure timeline tracked per SEC Cybersecurity Rules
Simultaneous public disclosure procedures (press release, 8-K, or other Reg FD-compliant channel) documented for inadvertent selective disclosure remediation
RS-02.framework_reference: SOX §302, §404; SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.101(e); SEC Cybersecurity Rules

evidence_requirements: Automated response playbooks for MNPI incidents include AI agent session termination, MNPI data quarantine, and access revocation procedures
Playbooks cover Reg FD-specific containment: immediate cessation of AI agent MNPI distribution and initiation of simultaneous public disclosure when required
Playbook testing conducted at defined cadence; test results reviewed by compliance and legal; playbooks updated following regulatory guidance changes
RS-03.framework_reference: SOX §802; SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.100(a); SEC Rule 17a-4

evidence_requirements: Recovery procedures for MNPI handling systems documented; restoration process verifies disclosure controls and access restrictions re-enabled before system returns to production
Business continuity plan covers AI agent MNPI workflow availability; recovery prioritizes disclosure control integrity over operational throughput
Recovery plan tested annually; test results document that MNPI safeguards verified as part of restoration process (SOX §404)
Post-incident review conducted following MNPI disclosure incidents; lessons learned documented and incorporated into governance and technical controls (SOX §404, §802)
Seven-year evidence preservation for MNPI incident records per SEC Rule 17a-4 and SOX §802 record-retention requirements; audit trail integrity verified post-incident
Control improvements from post-incident review implemented and tested; improvements documented in SOX internal control program with updated risk and control matrix

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: MNPI handling and disclosure-control evidence package aligned to SEC Reg FD selective-disclosure prevention, SOX internal controls, and seven-year record-retention support.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Issuer disclosure committee, legal/compliance leadership, investor relations, and audit committee or equivalent governance body.

human_oversight_mandates.description: The overlay does not impose a blanket human-in-the-loop flag, but SEC Reg FD and issuer disclosure controls require accountable human review before public dissemination, disclosure exceptions, or incident response decisions involving MNPI.

PR-05.regulatory_citation: SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.100-103; SOX §302, §404, §802; SEC Rule 17a-4

DE-01.regulatory_citation: SEC Reg FD 17 CFR 243.100(a); SOX §302, §404; SEC Rule 17a-4

notes: This overlay treats MNPI handling as a market-integrity and disclosure-control problem. SEC Reg FD drives selective-disclosure prevention and simultaneous-public-disclosure expectations, while SOX drives accountable internal controls and seven-year evidence retention for market-sensitive workflows.
